newsitem.title: GERMANY: German private broadcasters demand deregulation.
newsitem.headline: German private broadcasters demand deregulation.

text.p: German private broadcasters on Thursday accused government officials and media authorities of overregulating their industry while allowing print media more freedom in the advertising they carry.

The president of the Association of Private Broadcasting and Telecommunications (VPRT), Juergen Doetz, called for swift deregulation of the German market at the two-day Munich Advertising Conference, which will end on Thursday.
"We are still far from reaching our basic demand: the equal treatment of print media and broadcasters," Doetz said. "Instead we find ourselves in a regulatory jungle."

He pressed for an easing limits on the quantity and frequency of TV ads and the length of commercial breaks, as well as looser rules on sponsoring. He added it was now advertising that needed to be protected and not consumers.

"I call on law-makers to finally trust the market -- and that means the viewers of private television -- to decide with their remote controls if they want to support our programming or not," Doetz said.
Doetz also slammed a law before parliament which would limit the length of TV commercial blocks, saying shorter ad periods would bring private channels losses of 500 million marks a year.
In reference to still-developing EU media policy, Doetz urged Germany not to resist a trend toward more self-regulation by television stations he saw at the European level.

"Based on previous experience, we cannot expect that German policy will be the trailblazer of liberalisation," Doetz said. "However it is necessary to demand that it will not act as the brake on European liberalisation."
